newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASEAN will not follow EC route - economic director.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN will not follow EC route - economic director.

text.p: ASEAN is not likely to become a broad political federation along the lines of the European Community (EC), the director of the regional grouping's Bureau of Economic Co-operation said on Tuesday.

"(The Association of South East Asian Nations) is unlikely to adopt the European Community's model and evolve into an ASEAN common market with all the implications of forming a federal state and the adoption of a single currency," Chee Peng Lim said.
In a paper prepared for an ASEAN roundtable meeting in Singapore, Chee said closer cooperation between ASEAN members was desirable, but a supra-national bureaucracy was not.
The end of the Cold War had shifted the battle for global influence from political ideology to economic competitiveness, removing the need for stronger political and military ties.
"Economic strength is now more effective in determining a country's global status than military might," Chee said.

Creating an ASEAN economic area, accelerating freer trade in goods, services and investment, creating regional transport and communications links and boosting cooperation in the international macroeconomic arena should be priorities, he said.
This would also increase ASEAN's engagement with regional economic groups in the Pacific, Europe, Latin America and Africa.

"If ASEAN can realise its long-term vision, its achievements will enhance ASEAN's credibility so that its ability to speak in one voice in international trade negotiations will be taken seriously," Chee said.
